newsitem.title: USA: AOL passes 8 million members, ups spending.
newsitem.headline: AOL passes 8 million members, ups spending.

text.p: America Online Inc said that its membership has surpassed eight million members, as its unlimited pricing plan has attracted a record number of members, and it is also spending more to upgrade its network.
AOL said that it is increasing its investment in its network system expansion by $100 million, one day after it had a partial system outage of nearly four hours.
The world's largest online service said that it will increase its investment to $350 million, from $250 million, in order to deal with the extraordinary surge in demand for AOL.

AOL also said that it will sharply reduce its marketing activities in this quarter, as it continues to meet the needs of its current members. For the time being, AOL will stop airing its nationwide television advertising campaign, featuring the theme song from the Jetsons cartoon.
The company said it will also sharply reduce the number of mailings of free trial disks, especially to cities where its customers are experiencing the most severe busy signals.
AOL said that between now and June, it plans to increase the current total of its 200,000 plus modems in AOLNet by 75 percent. More system modems will let more consumers dial in.

AOL will also break ground next month on a 180,000 square foot data center. AOL also said it plans to seek other ways to increase capacity beyond these levels and is promoting and supporting alternate ways to get AOL through work or schools.
AOL also said it will add 600 additional customer support people over the next six months, bringing the total to 4,500.

Since AOL first switched its members to unlimited access for a flat rate of $19.95 a month on December 1, its system has been inundated with members, some of whom stay on the service all day, making it difficult for users to sign on during peak hours such as evenings and weekends.

In the past four days, mounting subscriber complaints have led to three different class action lawsuits filed against the company, with allegations ranging from breach of contract for failure to provide services to false advertising.
Attorneys general in several states have confirmed that they are in talks with AOL to seek some remedy to the growing consumer complaints they are receiving.

To add to its problems, late Wednesday afternoon, AOL had to shut down half its system when it noticed around 1500 EST that their computers were telling them that no new subscribers were able to sign on. They had to turn off part of the system which then ran at 50 percent capacity until 1930 EST.

AOL officials said that Wednesday's partial outage was not caused by the massive demand for its service. The company said that it took a few hours to find the problem because it had just done its bi-monthly system shut-down on Tuesday night, so there were more procedures to review in order to find the problem.
The problem turned out to be a glitch in an asynchronous transfer mode board that is placed in a router, which directs the flow of data on a network.
Once the board was replaced, AOL was able to turn the rest of the network back on and it was up and running at full capacity by 2000 EDT Wednesday.

In his monthly letter to members, Steve Case, AOL chairman and CEO, said,"I know that you have had great difficulty connecting to AOL in recent weeks, so I wanted to let you know what we're doing to address the problem. We all dial in from our homes at night, just like you do, so we see the problems firsthand...So are well aware of the extent of the problems. And we're working day and night to fix them."

AOL said the current usage of its network is exceeding its most aggressive forecasts, much of it due to the unlimited pricing plan. In December, its usage skyrockted to more than 100 million hours, up from 60 million hours in November.
